 American sets new revenue records amid historic fuel cost pressure 
 (English) (opens in new window) PDF 167 KB 
 FORT WORTH, Texas — American Airlines Group Inc. (NASDAQ: AAL) today 
reported its third-quarter 2026 financial results, reflecting execution of its 
commercial strategy and the benefits of long-term investments in its customers, 
team members, network, fleet and technology.
 Third-quarter financial highlights:
 Total revenue of $16.3 billion, up 19.3% year over year, above the high 
 end of the previously announced guidance range.
 Delivered the best unit cost performance among the network carriers, with 
 CASM-ex 1 up 3.0%.
 Fuel expense for the quarter increased $1.9 billion, or 67.5%, year over 
 year.
 GAAP net loss of $269 million, or ($0.41) per diluted share.
 Adjusted net loss of $182 million 2 , or ($0.28) per diluted 
 share. Adjusted net loss was only $71 million below third quarter 2025 
 despite the $1.9 billion increase in fuel expense.

 “American delivered record third-quarter revenue and the strongest 
 year-over-year revenue growth in my career, 
 with premium performance leading the way,” said American's CEO Robert Isom. 
 "The investments we are making across the four pillars of our commercial 
 strategy are working, and we expect another quarter of record revenue growth 
 to close out the year. While historically high fuel prices significantly 
 impacted our financial results, our focus remains on restoring profitability 
 and building a stronger American for the long term. I’m grateful to the 
 American Airlines team for making this progress possible.”
 The company’s third-quarter results were driven by strong revenue 
performance across all geographies and cabins:
 Premium revenue increased 22.9%, and Main Cabin revenue increased 19.5% 
 year over year.
 Total unit revenue increased 14.5% year over year, reflecting continued 
 strength in demand for travel.
 Domestic passenger unit revenue increased 13.6% year over year in the 
 third quarter.
 International passenger unit revenue increased 16.4%, with the Latin 
 America entity up 21.1%, the Atlantic entity up 14.5% and the Pacific entity 
 up 11.3% compared to the third quarter of 2025.
 AAdvantage ® enrollments increased 27.4% year over year.
 Demand for business travel remained strong, with managed corporate 
 revenue increasing 27.6% year over year, marking the sixth consecutive 
 quarter of double-digit growth.
 This revenue performance was a result of the company’s continued focus on 
its four commercial pillars: elevate the customer experience, grow the global 
network, drive premium revenue and lead in loyalty.
 1) Elevate the customer experience
 American’s investments in high-speed connectivity, lounges, seatback 
entertainment, airport facilities and fleet modernization are creating the 
foundation for a best-in-class customer experience.
 In May, American announced plans to equip more than 500 aircraft with 
high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi, representing the largest in-flight connectivity 
upgrade in the airline’s history. Building on that commitment, the company 
announced on Oct. 8 that it plans to expand Starlink installation across its 
entire mainline fleet, bringing the technology to more than 1,000 aircraft. 
Once installation is complete, American will offer one of the largest fleets of 
Starlink-connected aircraft in the world.
 The company also continues to grow its Admirals Club ® and premium 
lounge network with more lounges opening or being renovated than at any point 
in company history. Additionally, American announced the expansion of seatback 
entertainment to the narrowbody fleet, including screens on new deliveries 
beginning in 2028. With these foundational investments underway, American 
remains focused on further improving customer satisfaction through enhanced 
operational reliability, better disruption management and a more consistent 
travel experience.
 2) Grow the global network
 American continues to strengthen its global network, offering customers more 
destinations, better connectivity and greater schedule utility. At Dallas Fort 
Worth International Airport (DFW), this year's rebank produced record passenger 
volumes, fewer misconnections and mishandled bags, and unit revenue that 
outpaced the rest of the system. In Chicago, Miami, Philadelphia and Phoenix, 
American is building stronger schedules for local customers.
 3) Drive premium revenue
 American continues to see momentum in premium demand, demonstrating the 
benefits of recent investments across its premium products and customer 
experience. Premium passenger unit revenue increased 18.5% year over year 
during the third quarter, compared with an increase of 14.4% in Main Cabin.
 American plans to continue expanding premium seating through the delivery of 
new aircraft and the retrofit of existing aircraft. Premium products generate 
roughly half of the company's ticket revenue on approximately 30% of seats 
today. Through the recently announced narrowbody retrofit program, American 
expects premium seats on narrowbody aircraft to increase to 40% in the coming 
years.
 The company also continues to take actions to improve revenue quality and 
provide customers with a broader range of choices. These initiatives 
contributed to a 6-point increase in the upsell rate from Basic Economy to Main 
Cabin during the quarter.
 4) Lead in loyalty
 The AAdvantage ® program remains one of American's strongest 
competitive advantages, driving customer engagement, premium demand and 
long-term value creation. The program continues to benefit from strong member 
activity, increased engagement and enhancements to American’s co-branded credit 
card program.
 Enrollments in the AAdvantage ® program increased 27.4% year over 
year in the third quarter. American’s co-branded credit card partnership with 
Citi saw year-over-year third-quarter card spend growth of nearly 10%.
 Efficiency and cost performance
 American continues to benefit from long-term investments in technology, 
procurement and other initiatives designed to build a more efficient and 
resilient airline. The company is reengineering how work gets done across the 
business, improving productivity and simplifying processes while continuing to 
invest in the customer and team member experience.
 By the end of 2026, the company expects to have achieved nearly $1 billion 
in annual run rate savings and more than $900 million in working capital 
improvements through its multiyear reengineering efforts. American continues to 
identify opportunities to use technology, automation and artificial 
intelligence to simplify the business and equip team members with better tools 
to improve decision-making.
 “We remain focused on the factors that drive the most value,” said 
 American’s Chief Financial Officer Devon May. “Our long-term focus on efficiency 
 supported industry-leading unit cost results in the quarter, with 
 CASM-ex increasing 3.0% year over year. For the full year, we expect to 
 lead the network carriers in the spread between year-over-year unit revenue 
 and CASM-ex growth.”
 Overall financial results were pressured by a significant increase in fuel 
costs. American paid an average of $3.85 per gallon in the third quarter, which 
increased fuel expense by $1.9 billion year over year.
 Balance sheet and liquidity
 American ended the third quarter with $11.8 billion of total available 
liquidity and more than $26 billion of unencumbered assets and first-lien 
capacity. The company remains committed to reducing debt, lowering interest 
expense and achieving its target of 3.0x net debt 3 to EBITDAR, in 
line with BB credit metrics.
 Outlook and financial guidance
 In the fourth quarter, the company expects 
continued revenue strength, 
with year-over-year revenue growth between 19.5% and 22.5%. Based on the 
forward fuel curve as of Oct. 19, American anticipates an average fuel 
price of approximately $4.70 per gallon, nearly double the price paid 
in the fourth quarter of 2025. At that price, fuel expense is expected 
to increase approximately $2.8 billion versus the fourth quarter 
of 2025.
 Given elevated fuel prices, American expects network growth in 2027 to slow from 2026 levels.

 American will host a conference call at 7:30 a.m. CT today. A live webcast

 Notes
 See the accompanying notes in the financial tables section of this news 
release for further explanation, including reconciliations of certain GAAP to 
non-GAAP financial information.

 sharing, or CASM-ex, is a non-GAAP measure. The company is unable to

 amount of net special items cannot be determined at this time.
 Adjusted net loss is a non-GAAP financial measure and excludes $87 
 million of net special items after the effect of taxes that the company 
 recognized in the third quarter.
 Net debt includes debt, finance and operating lease liabilities and 
 pension obligations less unrestricted cash and short-term investments.
 Adjusted loss per diluted share guidance excludes the impact of net 
 special items and represents an absolute number, not a year-over-year 
 comparison. The company is unable to reconcile certain forward-looking 
 information to GAAP as the nature or amount of net special items cannot be 
 determined at this time.
 Other: Third-quarter revenue growth of 19.3% is the highest in company 
history excluding the years following the pandemic.

 About American Airlines Group (NASDAQ: AAL) 
American Airlines is a premium global airline connecting more of the U.S. to 
the world. With roots tracing back to an air mail carrier in the Midwestern 
United States in 1926, American now operates more than 6,000 daily flights to 
more than 350 destinations in more than 60 countries and serves more than 200 
million customers annually. Powered by a proud and talented team of 140,000 
aviation professionals, American’s team lives out the airline’s purpose of 
caring for people on life’s journey every day.
 The world’s largest airline proudly celebrates its centennial year in 2026, 
reaching a milestone that reflects a century of innovation and the Forever 
Forward SM spirit that changed the industry and the world. American 
introduced the first scheduled air cargo service, the first airport lounge and 
the first airline loyalty program and continues to reinvent the customer 
experience today. The airline is also a founding member of the 
 one world alliance, whose members serve more than 900 
destinations around the globe.
 Get the latest about American at news.aa.com and @AmericanAir .
